items.title: I stopped my Claude Code subagents from running on Fable instead of Sonnet
items.why_it_matters: Claude Code can sometimes spin up expensive or slower subagents by default. This guide shows you how to pin your subagent models to specific versions to keep your builds fast and your API costs predictable. This week, open your Claude Code configuration file and explicitly set your subagent model preferences to prevent unexpected API bill spikes.

items.title: Show HN: A pre-execution guard that stops AI agents running destructive commands
items.why_it_matters: When you let Claude Code run terminal commands, there is always a risk of it executing something destructive. This open-source pre-execution guard intercepts agent commands and blocks dangerous actions before they run. This week, clone the repo and set up the guard on your local machine so you can let Claude Code write and run commands on your AI-ingest project with zero anxiety.

items.title: Tokencompress A sub-2ms Go CLI and MCP sidecar that prunes AI agent tool context
items.why_it_matters: Claude Code uses Model Context Protocol (MCP) to talk to tools, which can quickly bloat your token usage and cost. Tokencompress is a fast MCP sidecar that automatically prunes unnecessary tool context before it gets sent to the model. This week, add the Tokencompress MCP server to your Claude Code configuration to instantly lower your token consumption and speed up your development loops.

items.title: Testing Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 Inside Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: Developers are successfully routing tasks inside Claude Code to alternative models like Moonshot's Kimi K3 to optimize API spend. This aligns with your goal of saving costs by delegating specific sub-tasks to cheaper, highly capable endpoints. This week, try configuring an alternative LLM provider in your Claude Code settings and run a simple feature generation task to see if you can cut your development costs.

items.title: Claude: System Prompts
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has officially published the system prompts they use to guide their Claude models. Reading these gives you a direct look at how the creators structure instructions for complex tasks like coding and tool use. This week, open the release notes, copy their prompt-structuring techniques, and use them to refine the system prompts in your Next.js app to make your AI features more reliable.
